recommended.confidence_rule: A 100% letter-for-letter match equals confidence 10 (100%). If one to three letters are off, and those differences are likely suffixes "ing", "ion", "ed", or "er", confidence remains high at 80–85%. After that, confidence of 75% or lower is unacceptable and results in writing unresolved domain. A confidence at or below 0.75 writes unresolved domain.
recommended.method: versioned local associative lexicon; no LLM calls; ranked multi-label evidence; if unresolvable, write unresolved domain; no forced symbol
recommended.rule_module: The actual rules for domain decisions will be an extensive module needing expansion, and will be an entire evening of work one day. For now, the current rule and lists will suffice. If unresolvable, write unresolved domain.
recommended.scoring_rubric: The professional TLD list at https://tld-list.com/tld-categories/professional is primary. If a domain exists on that list, it is domain-specific and tied to that .domain extension; a host of websites therefore exist from which terminology and structures can be extracted easily. If the domain is not part of the professional domain list, fall back to the attached NYCH taxonomy lexicon committed at icm/MG8PK/lexicons/nych-professional-domain-taxonomy.md. That lexicon will be updated with every proper NYCH update.
recommended.seed_lexicon: The professional TLD list at https://tld-list.com/tld-categories/professional is primary. If a domain exists on that list, it is domain-specific and tied to that .domain extension; a host of websites therefore exist from which terminology and structures can be extracted easily. If the domain is not part of the professional domain list, fall back to the attached NYCH taxonomy lexicon committed at icm/MG8PK/lexicons/nych-professional-domain-taxonomy.md. That lexicon will be updated with every proper NYCH update.
recommended.tie_policy: In the strange case of matching — a tie, when two or more domains receive the same score — include both (or all tied domains) and do not prune either domain. Instead use both as possible root domains and reason within both.

decisions.rationale: Owner approved the catalog v3.7 recommendation.

recommended.endpoint: The endpoint is the common emoji library. https://unicode.org/emoji/charts/full-emoji-list.html (Unicode Full Emoji List, v18.0). https://www.unicode.org/emoji/charts-18.0/ (Unicode Emoji Charts v18.0).
recommended.inputs: B5 GST and complete natural-language prompt as separate inputs
recommended.request_response_schema:
Symbol selection chooses an emoji/gestalt to represent each word, or compounds multiple words when they form a single idea.

If a compounded idea contains a name, the name-exclusion rule is ignored and the idea is compounded and embedded. Owner example: "fibbonacci sequence" embeds as `FbncSqnc`. The capitalized F indicates a name; the later capitalized S indicates a new word.

In normal gestalt selection, the shortened word is appended at the end of the id string, separated by `_`. Owner example: word becomes `_wrd`. If a second word is compounded to form a single idea, that second word is capitalized. Owner example: "word smith" becomes `wrdSmth`.

The chosen gestalt/emoji should best approximate the gestalt of the word. Owner examples: football = `ftbl` plus the ellipse-on-an-angle football emoji; hammer uses the hammer emoji. This will not always produce the most obvious gestalt; the word embedding gives enough of a clue to negate collisions and provide context by observing neighboring gestalt IDs.

A legend is printed atop the chat for domain-tree symbol mappings, because there are far more domains than emoji and unique choices cannot exist in an invariant lexicon. The current domain is identified and all subdomains are preserved. Gestalts as emoji are chosen according to the current domain. If the domain is switched, a marker is placed for indexing and the new legend is transmitted.

Invariants that never change per prompt or chat, and are universal to all NYCH uses and users, must be canonized in these contract terms: modality operators; narrative perspective and tense; time of day if any; and the grammatical invariants.

Everything that is not invariant is domain-selected. Unrelated domains are pruned until they are referenced by chat or inferred by actions.

At the point the LLM call is made to choose the gestalt emoji, NYCH symbols are chosen per word. This happens after the domain has been identified and the lookup has given subdomains and related structure. Those symbols are temporary or unique to this chat. They will eventually become normalized because of the legend and the LLM preference for stability. Per domain there will not be much variance, but some domains will require the same symbols. For example, computers and word processing may both use the computer-screen gestalt as the best match, and that symbol will represent something different in each domain. That on-the-fly sharing is the reason for choosing symbols this way.
recommended.tote_write_policy:
The modality operator is invariant and symbolic, but the TOTE loop database is inherently not symbolic, because symbols are chosen by domain. The TOTE loop library is the words organized in cells, rows, and columns: domain-specific, subdomain, and technique. Then the TOTE loop describes the technique with a minimum of 1 actor, 1 action, 1 object, and 1 modality operator.

Word organizing in the database will preserve the domain organization and the TOTE loop sequence, and allow all but the modality operators to be dynamically chosen.

recommended.abbreviation_to_gestalt_training: Part of training this model is training from word abbreviations to stabilized gestalt dynamics. This is unique to the NYCH language model.
recommended.attention_mixture: Attention weights the current ID and its neighbors as follows, as a starting mix: 30% the current gestalt, 30% the current abbreviated word, 20% neighboring gestalts, and 20% neighboring abbreviated words (the remaining 40% neighboring signal split 20/20). If that mix does not work, readjust the percentages and ratios. Adjust until optimal percentages and ratios are obtained through testing on natural language ("nat lang"). The 30% current gestalt / 30% current abbreviated word / 20% neighboring gestalts / 20% neighboring abbreviated words mix is the starting point, not a frozen optimum.
recommended.primacy_tradeoff: Until patterns are recognized from repetition, the abbreviated words appended on the gestalt ID string are primary. A tradeoff rule determines when the dynamic domain lexicons have stabilized; only then may the switch to symbolic (gestalt) primary be made. Words are not discarded; they remain appended on the ID string.

recommended.mixing_console: A dynamic mixing console adjusts these numbers in real time like an audio mixer and finds the intended balance. An AI may perform the mixing under human observation. The console does not have to be used to obtain the live parameters at first. The mix channels being balanced are the current gestalt, the current abbreviated word, neighboring gestalts, and neighboring abbreviated words, starting from the D8 mix of 30/30/20/20, plus the D9 block numbers (especially feed-forward width and training dropout) that affect how those signals are mixed. Inference dropout remains 0.0 and is not a mix channel.
recommended.repeatability: The console must produce repeatable outcomes. The same recipe — operator (human or AI observed), observation seed, mix-channel values, and D9 block settings — must yield the same mix and the same digest, and the same seed plus starting mix must replay the same observed AI moves.

recommended.verification_sidecar: The production D10 path still scores next NYCH tokens — gestalt IDs with the abbreviated word appended on the ID string — not full English words. To be sure that path is working, a parallel unmodified ("standard") version must ride the whole process alongside the abbreviated-word and gestalt mix as a faithfulness check. The mixed NYCH path should remain faithful if it is running alongside that proper unmodified companion. Once the D10 step is proven, delete the standard version. This sidecar is required verification, not an optional extra: it exists so the mixed path can be checked before it is trusted on its own.
